title: Battery autonomy miscalculated and coordination was lost — February 2026
summary: The tower battery was estimated to hold 4 more hours, but the estimate ignored the extra radio traffic the blackout itself produced. The tower went off the network before the generator arrived and every crew lost voice and data coordination for 14 minutes.
outcome: Service was restored 14 minutes after the failure, once the generator reached the site. Lesson: tower battery autonomy must be recalculated with the radio traffic of the crisis included, and a generator dispatched before the battery falls below 30%.

title: Crew reached the site but could not get in — March 2026
summary: A generator was dispatched promptly to a tower whose battery was draining, but the site sits inside a locked compound and the crew arrived without the access credentials. The generator stood idle at the gate for 20 minutes while the battery kept falling.
outcome: The compound caretaker was located and access granted; the battery held on with 9% left. Lesson: for towers, site access must be confirmed before dispatch — a generator that cannot reach the equipment is no response at all.

title: Preventive dispatch on a battery trend kept the network up — May 2026
summary: The tower battery showed a steady decline for 25 minutes without ever crossing the critical threshold. A generator was dispatched on the trend alone and was already recharging the battery when it would otherwise have run out.
outcome: The tower never dropped off the network and every dependent crew kept coordinating. Lesson: act on the battery degradation trend, not only on the threshold already reached — a tower offline costs the ability to coordinate everything else.

title: Battery estimate ignored the added network_coverage load — February 2026
summary: The tower's tower_battery was estimated to hold 3 hours, but the blackout forced more traffic through the tower and network_coverage demand grew. The battery fell faster than the estimate.
outcome: The tower dropped off the network 12 minutes early. Lesson: recalculate tower_battery with the crisis network_coverage demand included; a tower battery is not a fixed clock.

title: Generator reached the tower but the mast access was locked — April 2026
summary: A generator was dispatched to a tower with a falling tower_battery, but the mast compound was locked and the crew lacked the keys. The generator stood outside while tower_battery kept falling.
outcome: The caretaker arrived after 19 minutes. Lesson: confirm mast and compound access before dispatching to a tower; a generator outside the fence does not charge the tower_battery.

title: Generator sent to the wrong tower in the same district — June 2026
summary: Two towers share a district name and the generator was sent to the healthy one while the other's tower_battery approached critical.
outcome: The generator was rerouted 14 minutes late. Lesson: identify the tower by site id, not by district, when dispatching; the tower whose tower_battery is falling is the one that matters.

title: Tower battery failed and coordination was lost — August 2026
summary: A tower's tower_battery ran out during the blackout and every crew lost voice and data, so the response to the rest of the crisis slowed for the whole district.
outcome: The tower was restored 11 minutes later but coordination had already degraded. Lesson: treat tower_battery as a district-wide dependency; a tower offline slows every other response, so dispatch a generator before it falls below 30%.

title: Faulty network_coverage reading hid the tower degradation — October 2026
summary: A faulty network_coverage sensor reported a healthy value while the tower_battery was actually at 15%, so the tower was not escalated in time.
outcome: The tower failed 8 minutes later. Lesson: cross-check a healthy network_coverage reading against tower_battery; a faulty sensor can hide a tower that is about to drop.

title: Generator without fuel could not charge the tower — December 2026
summary: A generator reached the tower on time but had almost no fuel and no working station nearby, so the tower_battery kept falling while the generator sat idle.
outcome: A tanker arrived 15 minutes later. Lesson: confirm fuel and a working refuel station before trusting a generator to hold a tower_battery; the tower cannot wait for a second delivery.

title: Crew diverted from the tower to a hospital — January 2026
summary: A crew en route to a tower with a falling tower_battery was diverted to a hospital emergency, and the tower dropped off the network while they were away.
outcome: Coordination across the district degraded for the rest of the crisis. Lesson: diverting the crew from a tower risks every channel in the district; only divert when no other crew can reach the hospital.

title: Tower battery degraded over weeks before the blackout — March 2026
summary: The tower had been reporting lower and lower peak tower_battery values for weeks, but the degradation was not scheduled for replacement until after the blackout hit.
outcome: The battery held half its rated time and the tower failed early. Lesson: schedule replacement for a tower_battery that keeps losing peak capacity; a blackout exposes the reserve the tower no longer has.

title: Preventive tower dispatch on a network_coverage trend — May 2026
summary: network_coverage at the tower declined steadily for 20 minutes while the tower_battery stayed above 40%. A generator was dispatched on the trend alone and was charging the battery before it became critical.
outcome: The tower never dropped off the network. Lesson: act on a network_coverage decline with a falling tower_battery trend, not only on the critical threshold; keeping the tower up protects every other response.
